$$
\int_{0}^{1} 4 \cdot 3^{2 x^{2} + 2} x\,\mathrm{d}x
$$

{{answer}}"] [:db/add "012021b3-4d85-5cb3-8311-8b799e8be032" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=2 x^{2} + 2$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(4 x)\,\mathrm{d}x$.

Transform both bounds:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=0&\Longrightarrow u=2\\x=1&\Longrightarrow u=4\end{aligned}
$$

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int_{0}^{1} 4 \cdot 3^{2 x^{2} + 2} x\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\int_{2}^{4} 3^{u}\,\mathrm{d}u.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int 3^{u}\,\mathrm{d}u=\frac{3^{u}}{\ln{\left(3 \right)}}+C.
$$

Evaluate the primitive and subtract lower from upper:

$$
\left[\frac{3^{u}}{\ln{\left(3 \right)}}\right]_{2}^{4}=\left(\frac{81}{\ln{\left(3 \right)}}\right)-\left(\frac{9}{\ln{\left(3 \right)}}\right).
$$

The exact answer is

$$
\frac{72}{\ln{\left(3 \right)}}.
$$"] [:db/add "012021b3-4d85-5cb3-8311-8b799e8be032" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] [:db/add "012021b3-4d85-5cb3-8311-8b799e8be032" :question/answer-fields "119f5306-f073-5d16-91d6-d7cdf25e2a75"] [:db/ensure "012021b3-4d85-5cb3-8311-8b799e8be032" :question/validate] [:db/add 17592186184352 :knowledge-point/questions "012021b3-4d85-5cb3-8311-8b799e8be032"] [:db/add "2f77e899-5bf3-5606-be9d-9e74679a05f9" :answer/id #uuid "2f77e899-5bf3-5606-be9d-9e74679a05f9"] [:db/add "2f77e899-5bf3-5606-be9d-9e74679a05f9" :answer/type :answer.type/math] [:db/add "2f77e899-5bf3-5606-be9d-9e74679a05f9" :answer/value "\frac{2}{\ln{\left(2 \right)}}"] [:db/ensure "2f77e899-5bf3-5606-be9d-9e74679a05f9" :answer/validate] [:db/add "9d0908c6-1508-50e9-9268-c0821dfd898f" :answer-field/id #uuid "9d0908c6-1508-50e9-9268-c0821dfd898f"] [:db/add "9d0908c6-1508-50e9-9268-c0821dfd898f" :answer-field/key "answer"] [:db/add "9d0908c6-1508-50e9-9268-c0821dfd898f" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/blank] [:db/add "9d0908c6-1508-50e9-9268-c0821dfd898f" :answer-field/choices "2f77e899-5bf3-5606-be9d-9e74679a05f9"] [:db/add "9d0908c6-1508-50e9-9268-c0821dfd898f" :answer-field/correct "2f77e899-5bf3-5606-be9d-9e74679a05f9"] [:db/ensure "9d0908c6-1508-50e9-9268-c0821dfd898f" :answer-field/validate] [:db/add "1100c904-712f-5524-964a-421be8478f15" :question/id #uuid "1100c904-712f-5524-964a-421be8478f15"] [:db/add "1100c904-712f-5524-964a-421be8478f15" :question/problem "Evaluate exactly.

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int_{0}^{1} 2^{x + 1}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\int_{1}^{2} 2^{u}\,\mathrm{d}u.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\int 2^{u}\,\mathrm{d}u=\frac{2^{u}}{\ln{\left(2 \right)}}+C.
$$

$$
\left[\frac{2^{u}}{\ln{\left(2 \right)}}\right]_{1}^{2}=\left(\frac{4}{\ln{\left(2 \right)}}\right)-\left(\frac{2}{\ln{\left(2 \right)}}\right).
$$

$$
\frac{2}{\ln{\left(2 \right)}}.

{{answer}}"] [:db/add "e0fc7683-b8ed-592a-a25c-b785a2344d1a" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=x^{2}$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(2 x)\,\mathrm{d}x$.

Transform both bounds:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=0&\Longrightarrow u=0\\x=1&\Longrightarrow u=1\end{aligned}
$$

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int_{0}^{1} 4 \cdot 2^{x^{2}} x\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=2\left(\int_{0}^{1} 2^{u}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int 2^{u}\,\mathrm{d}u=\frac{2^{u}}{\ln{\left(2 \right)}}+C.
$$

Evaluate the primitive and subtract lower from upper:

$$
2\left(\left[\frac{2^{u}}{\ln{\left(2 \right)}}\right]_{0}^{1}\right)=2\left(\left(\frac{2}{\ln{\left(2 \right)}}\right)-\left(\frac{1}{\ln{\left(2 \right)}}\right)\right).
$$

The exact answer is
